title: Proper scalar comparison is invertible on bounded etale-origin inputs
statement: Let $p:Z\to Y$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $A\to B$ be a map of finite commutative rings. Use ordinary unbounded constant-ring module derived categories on the etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $E_e\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and assume $H_e=E_e\otimes_A^LB_{Z,\mathrm{et}}$ also lies in $D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Put $E=\nu_Z^*E_e$ with the canonical comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $S=-\otimes_A^LB$ and use the B-linear counit mate $\chi_{p,E}:S_YRp_*^AE\to Rp_*^BS_ZE$ of [lem-fix-proetale-scalar-mate-normalization]. Then $\chi_{p,E}$ is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. More precisely, under the scalar-restriction identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], its scalar restriction is $\nu_Y^*$ of the actual etale projection arrow $Rp_*E_e\otimes_A^LB_{Y}\to Rp_*(E_e\otimes_A^LB_{Z})$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], conjugated by the canonical tensor comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the counit-mate direct-image comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] at $E_e$ and $H_e$ (p is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, being proper). No flatness or finite projective dimension of B over A is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F0G, lemma-projection-formula-proper-mod-n; transport through the counit-mate etale/pro-etale comparisons

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $p$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Set $N=B_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$, regarded as a constant $A$-module in degree zero, and use [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] for the geometric inverse images $p_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ and $\nu_T^*$: canonically $p_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}N=B_{Z,\mathrm{et}}$ and $\nu_T^*B_{T,\mathrm{et}}=B_{T,\mathrm{proet}}$. Thus the object $L=E_e\otimes_A^Lp_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}N$ is $H_e$. Both $E_e$ and $L$ are bounded below by hypothesis. These are exactly the two boundedness assumptions in [lem-sfb-projection-comparison-etale-proetale]; no boundedness of a tensor of $Rp_*E_e$ is being inferred.

source.place: Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison, hypotheses; constant objects: sites.tex Tags 0H7J and 00YV

proof.text: The finite additive group of $A$ has a positive exponent, so $A$ is a torsion ring. Apply [lem-kun-0f0g] to $p$, $E_e$, and $N=B_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$. It says that the actual counit-defined projection arrow $\pi_e:Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}E_e\otimes_A^LN\to Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}H_e$ is invertible. This theorem allows unbounded inputs and does not require $N$ to be flat or perfect. Its arrow is the arrow of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], rather than an unspecified isomorphism of the endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0F0G, lemma-projection-formula-proper-mod-n; named arrow from sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0B56

proof.text:
Use the notation of [lem-sfb-projection-comparison-etale-proetale] with $K=E_e$, $N=B_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$ and $L=H_e$: $F_T=\nu_T^*$, $R_e=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$, $R_p=Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}$, $a:F_Zp_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\simeq p_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}F_Y$, $t_T:F_T(-\otimes_A^L-)\simeq F_T(-)\otimes_A^LF_T(-)$, and $h=(1\otimes a_N)t_{Z;E_e,p_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}N}$. Its equality is
$$R_p(h)b_{H_e}F_Y(\pi_e)=\pi_p(b_{E_e}\otimes1)t_{Y;R_eE_e,N}.$$
Here $\pi_p$ is precisely the ordinary $A$-linear pro-etale projection arrow at $(E,B_Y)$. The comparisons $b_{E_e},b_{H_e}$ are the counit-normalized mates of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The comparisons $t_T$ are the canonical derived tensor isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus the displayed equality uses exactly the comparisons specified in the item.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, specialized to the etale/pro-etale square; projection comparison node states the resulting named-map equation

proof.text:
Solve the equation in step 3 by composing on the right with $t_{Y;R_eE_e,N}^{-1}(b_{E_e}^{-1}\otimes1)$:
$$\pi_p=R_p(h)b_{H_e}F_Y(\pi_e)t_{Y;R_eE_e,N}^{-1}(b_{E_e}^{-1}\otimes1).$$
Every factor is invertible: $h$ is a composite of tensor and pullback isomorphisms, the two $b$'s are invertible at the bounded-below objects from step 1, and $\pi_e$ is invertible by step 2. Functors and tensoring take an inverse to an inverse. Consequently $\pi_p$ is invertible, with precisely this conjugation formula.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram; elementary rearrangement of the equation in step 3

proof.text: For the B-linear mate $\chi_{p,E}$ specified in the statement, [lem-fix-proetale-scalar-mate-normalization] identifies its scalar restriction, using the canonical tensor and direct-image restriction identifications, with the same $\pi_p$. Therefore the formula in step 4 is also the required formula for the scalar restriction of $\chi_{p,E}$; in particular that restriction is invertible. Apply the conservativity assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $R_T=A_T$, $S_T=B_T$ and their canonical constant-coefficient structural identifications. It reflects this isomorphism, proving that $\chi_{p,E}$ itself is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. The normalization has no flatness or boundedness hypothesis, and the only boundedness used above was that of $E_e,H_e$.
